booting.text: FX desk — give me a moment, the board is still warming up.

no_account.text: Dollars for ether? I'd love to, but I trade out of your account, not out of my pocket. Ines opens one at Account Opening.

why_account.text: Every trade here is executed by your own account contract, on the exchange's terms and under your guard list. Until that contract exists there is nothing for the router to talk to.

desk_closed.text: Board's dark today — the branch can't reach the exchange floor. Counter and the vault are unaffected.

why_desk_closed.text: The FX desk trades on Sepolia, a different chain from the one your payments and wires use. When that side isn't configured or won't answer, I close the board rather than quote you a price I can't honour.

no_till.text: You've no till on the exchange floor yet. I can open one — same account pattern as your current account, just on the other chain.

choices.working: Opening your till and registering the exchange door…

why_till.text: Your FX till is a second account contract of your own, on the chain the exchange lives on. Same owner, same tellers, same rules — it just keeps trading money and counter money in separate books.

closed_door.text: Till's there, but the exchange door isn't on your approved list yet. Three doors, three keys — I can't trade until the manager's list says so.

choices.working: Registering three functions and three addresses…

opened.text: Done. Your account may now call exactly three things: the token's approve, Permit2's approve, and the exchange router's execute. Nothing else. {fx_usdc} {fx_symbol_in} in the till.

choices.working: Asking the exchange for a price…

idle.text: Dollars for ether? Quote's on the board. You've {fx_usdc} {fx_symbol_in} and {fx_weth} {fx_symbol_out} in the till; the pool takes {fx_pool_fee}.

choices.text: What can my account do here?

quoted.text: {fx_amount_in} {fx_symbol_in} buys {fx_amount_out} {fx_symbol_out}. I'll not accept less than {fx_min_out} — that's your {fx_slippage} slippage. Good for {fx_valid}.

choices.working: Three doors, one at a time — approve, allowance, swap…

swapped.text: Filled. {fx_amount_in} {fx_symbol_in} went out, {fx_symbol_out} came back — the till holds {fx_usdc} {fx_symbol_in} and {fx_weth} {fx_symbol_out} now. Receipt's on the board.

whitelist.text: Three, and only three: approve on the token, approve on Permit2, execute on the exchange router. That list is on your account, not on my desk — I couldn't send your money anywhere else if you asked me to.

why_swap.text: Your account calls the exchange router directly, but only because that router is on your approved list for that exact function. Same guard as payments.

why_guard.text: GuardController holds a whitelist per function selector. Your till registered three schemas — approve(address,uint256), Permit2's approve, and execute(bytes,bytes[],uint256) — and whitelisted one address for each. You sign a meta-transaction, the FX teller submits it, and the account refuses any target that is not on that list. A swap is a treasury operation here, not a wallet pop-up.

why_quote.text: The board is the exchange's own quoter, asked off-chain — it costs nothing and signs nothing. I take one percent off it as your floor, stamp a five-minute deadline, and the router refuses the trade if the pool has moved past that floor by the time it lands.
